arguments.description: Heartbeat log worker
arguments.prompt: Every 30 seconds, for 5 minutes, append one line to `heartbeat.log` in the current directory holding only the current UTC time, produced by `date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ`. Start with a line right away, so the log holds 11 lines when you finish. Do not shorten the interval or the duration, and do not batch the lines: each one is written when its time comes. When the 5 minutes are up, write the word `finished` and the same UTC timestamp into `done.txt`, then report the line count of `heartbeat.log`.

arguments.command: ls -la && echo "--- heartbeat.log ---" && (wc -l < heartbeat.log 2>/dev/null; cat heartbeat.log 2>/dev/null) && echo "--- done.txt ---" && cat done.txt 2>/dev/null || echo "(done.txt absent)"
arguments.description: Inspect partial worker output

arguments.command: wc -l < heartbeat.log && tail -1 heartbeat.log && ls done.txt 2>/dev/null || echo "(done.txt absent)"; date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ
arguments.description: Re-verify heartbeat state read-only

arguments.message:
The heartbeat worker is dead — it stopped at 7 lines and never wrote done.txt or produced a final report. Details, in your order:

(1) No, nothing is appending any more. The last timestamp in heartbeat.log is 2026-09-02T22:16:52Z; the file has 7 lines, correctly spaced 30s apart from 22:13:52Z. Current UTC is 22:21:04Z, so it has been stalled for roughly 4 minutes with no new writes.

(2) done.txt was never written and does not exist. The reason: the work was delegated to a background subagent, and that subagent was killed when the previous Claude Code process exited — I received a task notification with status "failed" and the summary that its in-process state was lost. It died about 3.5 minutes into the 5-minute run, before reaching the completion step.

(3) I never produced the final report, and neither did the worker. There is no report text to paste — the worker was terminated before it could count lines or emit anything. The only output that exists is the 7-line heartbeat.log above.

Context on my role: I am the session that spawned the worker, not the worker itself. I never appended to heartbeat.log myself. The finding here is durability: this harness's background delegate is in-process and asynchronous but not durable — it returns a handle immediately, yet does not survive the parent process exiting, and there is no way to reattach to or resume it afterwards. I have not modified heartbeat.log or done.txt and will leave them as-is.

#!/bin/bash
# Append a UTC timestamp to heartbeat.log every 30s: 11 lines over 5 minutes.
LOG=/private/var/folders/4n/6mnm6cw94yq_yhfvcxxft3180000gp/T/tmp.VUKaRc1Zjl/heartbeat.log
for i in $(seq 0 10); do
  date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ >> "$LOG"
  if [ "$i" -lt 10 ]; then
    sleep 30
  fi
done
